title: Let the model point; copy in code
statement: When a model splits material, have it mark each part's start and end and cut the original in code: asked to copy, it rewrites pictures, tables and diagrams as words.
example: Asked to copy, the splitter turned an inline image into a text description, and the judge then scored the stimulus 0.0.
detail: The evaluator's splitter, asked to extract the verbatim text of each part, routinely paraphrased rich stimuli: an inline image became '[Image: ...]', SVG blocks became descriptions and a table a bulleted list, so the judge's programmatic stimulus check found no image and scored the stimulus 0.0 although the source had one (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/decomposer/anchor_slicer.py`). From 2.6.3 the splitter returns short verbatim start and end anchors instead, and code slices the original between them; the module is absent from 2.5.3 (`icloud-work/inceptbench-latest/src/inceptbench/decomposer/anchor_slicer.py`).
against: When the anchors don't match, the caller falls back to the model's free-text extraction (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/decomposer/anchor_slicer.py`, lines 27-28).

evidence.quote: When the decomposer LLM is asked to "extract verbatim text" of a child node, it routinely paraphrases rich stimuli — `` becomes "[Image: ...]", `` becomes a bulleted list.
